deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page): b is a von Neumann algebra (ring of operators) with a faithful normal semifinite trace T, and a is the ideal of T-integrable (or T-finite) elements. For A >= 0 in b, the previous page defined phi_A, the decreasing 'rearrangement' or spectral function of A on R+*: the generalized singular value function, with phi_A(0+) = ||A||. Following the commutative model f -> phi_f, it then defined Phi_A(t) = int_0^t phi_A(s) ds and Psi_A(t) = int_0^t log phi_A(s) ds.

This page extends the definitions to arbitrary A in b via the modulus |A| = (A*A)^{1/2}:
(5) Delta_A(t) = Delta_{|A|}(t) = Delta_{phi_{|A|}}(t) = exp int_0^t log phi_{|A|}(s) ds.
(6) Delta(A) = Delta_A(omega), where omega = T(1), whenever T(1) < +infinity.
When T is finite and normalized, Delta(A) = exp T(log|A|), which is exactly the Fuglede-Kadison determinant, here written as a rearrangement integral. For a semifinite trace one only has the one-parameter family Delta_A(t), a 'determinant up to level t'.

A struck passage records elementary properties. Delta_A(t) is a continuous function of t with finite values bounded in terms of ||A||; Delta(A) is defined when T(1) < infinity, with a finiteness bound.

Grothendieck then starts a new topic: the commutative case. If b is commutative, b = C_0(M) (or L^infinity), with T given by a measure on M. A point t in M of positive measure corresponds to a minimal projection U_{t}, and E is decomposed as a union over such atoms. Most of the lower half is struck through. It seems to work toward characterising minimal projections and atoms; the next page continues with a decomposition of the algebra into a type I (atomic, L(H)-like) part and a remainder via minimal projections E with T(E) < infinity.

Vertical margin: a note to 'define' something like int f dmu/(1+f...) and a quantity W(A), with the word 'Dual'. This is possibly a planned duality or Orlicz-type functional; it is unreadable in detail.

Purpose: this is the drafting of what became Grothendieck's Bourbaki seminar talk 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace' (1955). There he transfers rearrangement and convexity inequalities (Hardy-Littlewood-Pólya, Weyl/Horn type) to semifinite von Neumann algebras via phi_A, Phi_A and the determinant.
errors: The struck bound 'Delta_A(t) <= ||A||' should be Delta_A(t) <= ||A||^t, since log phi_{|A|} <= log ||A||. The writing is ambiguous and the passage is crossed out anyway.

Delta_A(t) may equal 0 when log phi_{|A|} is not integrable near t, so the struck lower bound (read by the machine as '1 <= Delta(A)') is wrong as transcribed. It is presumably '0 <= Delta(A) < +infinity'.
Continuity of Delta_A(t) in t holds as a map to [0, infinity) (exp of a monotone integral, extended by 0); this needs a remark at the first t where the integral diverges to -infinity.

ideas.what: Determinant function Delta_A(t) = exp int_0^t log mu_s(A) ds for an operator in a semifinite von Neumann algebra, via the generalized singular value function
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fuglede-Kadison (1952) for the finite case; Fack-Kosaki (1986) for the systematic generalized s-number formalism; Grothendieck's 1955 Bourbaki talk as an early source
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955), 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace'

ideas.what: Delta(A) = Delta_A(T(1)) recovers the Fuglede-Kadison determinant for finite traces
Commutative von Neumann algebra as C_0(M)/L^infinity; atoms (points of positive measure) correspond to minimal projections, leading to an atomic (type I) versus diffuse decomposition
ideas.modern_name: Atomic/diffuse decomposition; minimal projections and type I summands

missed.claim: This is the draft stage of Grothendieck's 1955 rearrangement/determinant theory for semifinite traces. It shows that the one-parameter determinant Delta_A(t) for semifinite (not just finite) algebras was explicitly set up by 1953, predating Fack-Kosaki by over 30 years. This is documentary priority only; the published Bourbaki talk already contains the core.
missed.quote: Delta_A(t) = Delta_{|A|}(t) = Delta_{phi_{|A|}}(t) = exp int_0^t log phi_{|A|}(s) ds ; Delta(A) = Delta_A(omega) (si omega = T(1) < +infinity)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor historical attribution for generalized s-numbers and determinants in semifinite algebras (used in L^2-invariants and the Brown measure); it is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the semifinite Fuglede-Kadison determinant via singular value functions, which Grothendieck published in his 1955 Bourbaki talk. The commutative/atom discussion is routine and mostly crossed out, and the margin note on W(A)/'Dual' is too illegible to assess.
transcription_corrections: The line beginning 'Supposons que E soit...' likely reads 'Supposons que b soit un anneau d'opérateurs commutatif...' ('b' or 'C', not 'E', at the start); this is uncertain.
The struck line 'Par construction, Delta_A(t) est une fonction continue de t à valeurs ... <= ||A||' may contain ||A||^t.
The struck '1 <= Delta(A) < +infinity' is more plausibly '0 <= Delta(A) < +infinity'.
In (6) the scribbled-over symbol before Delta_A(omega) is a deleted 'lim' or similar; the intended formula is Delta(A) = Delta_A(omega) with omega = T(1).
